A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ACTIONPIECE and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–E. Corresponding material can be matched despite changes in pagination and placement.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on mode discovery, density estimation, chunk transfer, tokenizer choice, and sample diversity, including appendix results.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds evaluated Option-Critic and WordPiece comparisons.

M1.justification: Appendix D newly evaluates a WordPiece variant, changing the tokenizer used to construct chunks. This is a limited procedural alternative: the default BPE pipeline, Increment/Replace mechanisms, action encoder, replay buffer, and ShortParse policy remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate FractalGrid, RNA sequence generation, bit sequences, and graph generation, including the same RNA transfer scenarios and longer-sequence settings in the appendices. No dataset, domain, or task coverage is added or removed.

E2.justification: Figure 2 adds Option-Critic to the existing mode-discovery comparisons. Table 3 adds its RNA result and WordPiece tokenizer comparisons. WordPiece was described in v1's related work but was not evaluated there; the existing comparators remain.

E3.justification: The added Option-Critic experiments introduce settings including 10 options and a 0.01 termination regularization coefficient in Appendices B.1–B.3. The retained experiments' training budgets, reward functions, chunking schedules, and evaluation metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix D extends the existing BPE-versus-uniform tokenizer ablation with WordPiece under both chunking mechanisms. This broadens the test of tokenizer dependence. The latent-structure, compression, transfer, and reward-diversity analyses already appear in v1.

E5.justification: Figure 2 newly identifies shaded bands as standard deviations across six seeds; Table 2 adds a six-seed statement, and Figure 4 displays six seeds separately instead of aggregate bars with error bars. Corresponding earlier run counts are unspecified, so an explicit increase in runs is not established.

E6.justification: The quantitative mode-discovery evidence is substantially revised. Figure 2 reverses the reported GFlowNet-Replace versus A2C-Replace ordering on the 128-bit task. Table 3 changes existing aggregates, including GFlowNet Atomic from 43.24±2.21 to 47.12±4.18, and adds WordPiece and Option-Critic results. These are revised reports, not demonstrated gains from a changed core method. Density-estimation and transfer results are retained.

T1.justification: The DAG assumptions, trajectory-balance mathematics, ShortParse recurrence and Markovian-factorization proof, and sampling-metric derivations are unchanged. The added explanation of amortized sampling is conceptual rather than a new formal result.

C1.justification: The abstract qualifies learned chunks as 'potentially interpretable' instead of 'interpretable.' The expanded conclusion emphasizes benefits with diversity-seeking samplers. The central claims concerning action abstraction, mode discovery, density estimation, and transfer remain.

C2.justification: Appendix D adds conclusions about tokenizer dependence and WordPiece performance. The conclusion expands discussion of interactions between exploration and library quality, while Appendix B.4 proposes rules or human feedback for explicitly encouraging interpretability. Existing explanations of RL mode concentration remain.

D1.justification: Appendices B.1–B.3 add Option-Critic network architectures, learning rates, and entropy and termination settings. The documented code location changes from an anonymous repository to the named Chunk-GFN GitHub repository, also linked in the abstract. Existing hardware and runtime disclosures remain.

R1.justification: v2 adds Zheng et al.'s PRISE and distinguishes its offline, static macro-action library in continuous control from ACTIONPIECE's online library updates. The conclusion further situates the contribution within macro-action research and diversity-seeking RL; most related work is retained.

P1.justification: v2 adds an introductory explanation of amortized sampling, expands the conclusion, rewrites the tokenizer discussion, and revises front matter and acknowledgements. The main section sequence and most explanatory prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 4 is redrawn with separate seed bars, Figure 2 gains an Option-Critic legend entry, and Table 3 gains columns and a row. Several displays are resized or relocated, and Listing 1 is restyled. The overall layout and most figures remain recognizable.

improvement.justification: The added Option-Critic and WordPiece comparisons make the evaluation more informative, while explicit seed reporting and the revised Figure 4 improve transparency. Qualifying interpretability also better calibrates the claims. These gains are limited by overgeneralized tokenizer conclusions—Uniform still outperforms both learned tokenizers for A2C-Replace—and an apparent new Table 3 uncertainty typo, printed as ±180.
